name: Mount Mary Basilica
blurb: A hilltop basilica on a rock, reached by a broad flight of steps, with the whole western skyline underneath.
description: Built into a rock above the Bandstand, with a broad staircase from the road, a long nave, and a covered walkway along the cliff edge. The terrace at the top is the reason people come and it is the flattest part. Step-free via a side ramp; the main steps are the obvious approach and there are about seventy of them.

name: Bandstand, Walkeshwar
blurb: A stone terrace over the sea at the north end of the promenade, and the sunset crowd faces the wrong way on purpose.
description: A nineteenth-century sea terrace with a wide, flat, walled edge over the water. The crowd photographs the city behind them rather than the sunset in front, which is the whole joke. Completely flat, benches along the wall, and the connecting Bandstand path is the smoothest walking surface in the whole of Bandra.

activities: walking the flat path to Mount Mary

__meta.note: `accessibility.restroomOnSite: false` is curated — no public toilets at the Bandstand.

name: BDD Chawl
blurb: A kilometre of a 1920s workers' chawl on one side of a road and none on the other. Look up, then look at the doors.
description: One of the few surviving chawl blocks, with the long open corridor, the columns, the shared courtyard, and laundry on the balconies. You can walk straight down the middle, which is unusual. Flat throughout, and residents are used to visitors walking through; the courtyard is a working space, not a museum.

name: Sea Princess viewpoint, Bandra
blurb: Everyone photographs the Sea Princess from the road and almost nobody goes past it. The ground beyond is open, flat, and empty.
description: A famous 1960s hotel on the rocks, seen from the promenade by everybody. The land behind and below it is open ground that you can actually walk onto, and it is one of the few flat empty spaces on this coast. No shelter, no toilets, and no point going in bad light.

name: St. Andrew's Church, Bandra
blurb: A white Protestant church from the 1860s, a bandstand beside it, and a graveyard that is the quietest place in Bandra West.
description: One of the oldest surviving buildings in Bandra, with a painted ceiling and a graveyard out the back under trees. The lawn and the graves are flat, cool, and about as calm as Bandra gets. Step-free throughout, and the only church here with toilets.

name: Hill Road
blurb: A ridge road between two rail lines with the sea on one side and the station on the other, and a flyover you can walk under.
description: A long, gently curving road above Bandra with the Western Line cutting across underneath and the sea opening up on the west side. The gradient is gentle, the surface is good, and the flyover at the top gives shade. It becomes a vehicular mess at seven and eleven, so go in the middle of the day or at dawn.

name: Hill Road Persian market
blurb: Iranian shops selling bread, sweets and pickles on a Bandra hill road. Cheaper than you expect, and the bread is the reason to go.
description: A run of Persian shops that grew around an old Zoroastrian cemetery, now a food street selling pita, lashani and felfeli, plus an unreasonable quantity of sweets. Level pavement on the main stretch, shop thresholds you have to step over, and a pavement that gets busy from seven in the evening.

name: Hill Road Sunday market
blurb: Sunday only, along the same road, and it is a completely different use of the space. Not worth a trip; worth the walk if you are already here.
description: Trestle tables down the middle of the road on Sunday morning: clothes, plants, junk, and a food section at the end. Packed by ten, gone by one, and the pavement narrows to a strip. Level in principle; in practice you will be in a moving crowd with a stroller.

activities: eating at the end of the row

name: Bandra Fort (Castella de Aguada)
blurb: Portuguese ruins on a hill above the village, with a cannon and a very steep approach. The ruins are the reward for the climb.
description: A small Portuguese-era fortification on a rocky hill, mostly foundations and two vaults, reached by a steep stone road or a set of steps. What survives is worth the climb and what does not is a lot of rubble. No shade, no water, no toilets, and a gradient that rules out a wheelchair or a walking frame.

name: Linking Road flea
blurb: Second-hand clothes and houseware spread along a whole street, most of it outside. Sunday mornings are the busiest hour.
description: A long stretch of street trading in second-hand clothing, crockery and odd furniture, most of it on the pavement with tarpaulins. You can walk the whole thing on level ground and the goods are genuinely cheap, but the crowd density on a Sunday is high. Not a good choice for anyone who finds crowds difficult.

name: Koli community morning, Versova
blurb: Boats landing at first light, a Koli family explaining the catch, and breakfast afterwards. Eight people, booked a day ahead.
description: A Koli family takes visitors out to the landing at first light to watch the boats come in, then cooks what was landed. It is the only genuine community-hosted experience in the four areas, and it is a real commitment from a real family, so the group is eight and it must be booked. The ground is sand, mud and rock; there is no step-free route and no toilet.

__meta.note: Koli communities around Versova and Bandra are real and community visits are offered. This specific programme, family, price and booking window are invented for the demo. `requiresJourney: true` because the journey is most of it.

name: Dhobi Lane viewpoint
blurb: Laundry, open drains, and the coloured roofs of Bandra below. Photographic, not pleasant, and the ground is wet and broken.
description: A working dhobi lane on the Bandra side where washing is beaten in vats and hung on lines overhead, with a view across the roofs towards the sea. It smells, the ground is wet and broken, and there are open drains. Photographers come for the lines and the colour; nobody comes for the experience. Do not send a wheelchair user or a toddler. Closed Sunday, when the dhobis rest.

__meta.note: Included as an explicit negative-quality record: a real kind of attraction that most products would recommend. It exists so the engine has something honest to reject on `strollerOk`/`lowStairs`, and so the reviews can carry negative sentiment.

name: The Mews studio
blurb: Ninety minutes with an artist in a working studio, on the second floor of a lane building. Six people, no glass wall.
description: A painter opens the studio and talks through one work while you sit with tea and ask questions. Six people only, no observation window, and no obligation to buy. The stairwell is a proper narrow one with a turn and no lift, so a wheelchair is not possible; the second-floor room itself is fine once you are up.

name: The ceramicist's kiln day
blurb: Two and a half hours throwing, trimming, and loading a kiln. Five people, and you cannot collect the piece for three weeks.
description: A full throwing session on a wheel, then trimming the foot, then a kiln loading with the studio's own work. Dust, noise, aprons, and a genuinely hard two and a half hours on your feet. Five places. Wheelchairs cannot reach the wheel bench because of the fixed layout, and the piece is fired and collected weeks later, so it does not work as an in-window activity for anyone who wants to leave with the thing.

name: The vinyl room
blurb: One turntable, a wall of records, and a selector who will play anything you ask for if you are patient.
description: A small second-floor room where a selector plays records all night, mostly soul, jazz and Goan 45s, taking requests. Twenty people, a stairwell that is steep but short, and a sound system that is genuinely loud by the second hour. No food beyond chips, and the toilets are in the building's shared block one floor down.

name: Persian sweet house, Hill Road
blurb: A glass counter of saffron sweets, thirty rupees a piece, and a queue out of the door on Fridays.
description: A small sweets counter with a glass front and a room behind with six tables. Lozenge, sohan, and felfeli sold by weight; the room is clean, brightly lit, and a genuine refuge from the lane. No toilets, and the queue starts at one on Fridays and Saturdays.

name: Goan kitchen off Hill Road
blurb: Fish curry, rice, and a kitchen that has been doing the same three things for thirty years. One room, twenty covers.
description: A family-run Goan kitchen in a first-floor room above a shop, with a short menu written on a board. Slow, generous, and the fish is genuinely good rather than an afterthought. The stair is a single flight with a turn, but the room beyond is level and the food is the point.

name: Sukoon, Bandra West
blurb: A restaurant that takes children seriously, has a step-free entrance, and does not mind noise. Rare on that combination.
description: A bright all-day restaurant with a small indoor play corner, high chairs that actually exist, and a menu that includes something mild for a child who will not eat anything brown. Noisy, busy, and expensive relative to the neighbourhood, but it is the record that should surface for a family with a toddler and a per-person ceiling. Step-free, toilets on site, and a change of space for a two-year-old.

activities: a long lunch with a toddler

name: Bandra street art walk
blurb: Forty-odd murals across six lanes, most of them above head height, and half the art is gone and repainted within a year.
description: A self-guided walk of a dozen documented murals across the back lanes, with a downloadable map. Art changes constantly, so the map is a snapshot and some of it will be painted over. Level throughout, and the lanes are quiet, which is unusual for Bandra.

name: Above the Western Line, Pali Hill
blurb: A footpath above the railway with trains going past underneath and the whole city on one side. Ninety minutes, and the trains are the point.
description: A walking path on the Pali Hill side of the Western Line where you look down on trains running both directions, with the skyline beyond. Unpaved in places and uneven, so it is a bad choice for a stroller or a walking frame, and there is nothing to buy and nowhere for a toilet. Best at six in the evening when the line is busiest.

__meta.note: Path above the Western Line around Pali Naka. Approximate position; reconcile with the OSM snapshot. Included because the isochrone reference data covers `pali_hill`, so travel-time estimates for it are real rather than estimated.

name: Old Bandra cinema foyer
blurb: The foyer of a 1950s cinema, preserved down to the ticket window, and nobody uses it for anything now.
description: A shuttered single-screen cinema kept as a memory: the original ticket window, the staircase to the circle, the hand-pilled poster frames, and the projection booth glass. Volunteers open it on request, so it is not a walk-in and you should not build a plan around it without checking. Flat, dry, and quiet.

name: Bandra village church bells
blurb: The evening bell across Bandra village, five minutes, no building required. Small, odd, and free.
description: At five the bell goes across the village and everybody stops. There is no tour, no ticket, and nothing to enter; you either stand in the lane and listen or you do not. Useful as an honest five-minute entry in a plan, and a way of making a Bandra plan feel like a place rather than a list.

name: Sunday organ at the Bandra church
blurb: A short organ recital on a mechanical tracker, no amplification, and a congregation that has heard it for a century.
description: A 70-minute programme on a tracker organ in a nineteenth-century church, played before the service. No microphone, which is the point and also why it is loud in a small room. Level access, toilets on site, and free seating at the back if you arrive early.

__meta.note: `accessibility.hearingLoop: false` is curated: a mechanical tracker organ has no amplification and therefore no induction loop. It is set explicitly so the compound-need scenario has a real negative.

name: Bandra kite festival
blurb: One weekend in the season, on a flat field, with two hundred people and about four hundred kites. The best two hours in Bandra for a family.
description: A one-weekend kite festival on a reserved open field, with a food stall row, a kite-making tent, and a children's section. Entry covers the field only. Level, fenced, toilets on site, and it is the only genuinely good large outdoor event option for a family with a toddler in this part of the city.

__meta.note: A kite festival at this scale is a real kind of event in Mumbai, but this instance, dates, field and capacity are invented. See content/events/events.jsonl for the event rows with the same disclaimer.

name: Versova harbour boat morning
blurb: Two hours out into the fishing harbour in a hired trawler, with the auction happening alongside you.
description: A trawler hired for ten people, going out past the last jetty into the harbour where the fish auction is under way, then back along the coast. Life jackets provided and the sea state is checked first, so it gets cancelled. Boarding is across a stone step down to a moving deck, so no wheelchair and no small children.

__meta.note: Boat trips out of Versova exist; this specific route, vessel and price are invented. `weatherSensitive: any` and the 120-minute duration make it the obvious candidate for a rain replan swap.

name: Hill Road tea stall
blurb: Cutting chai, sixty rupees, and a steel bench along the wall. Twenty minutes, and the cheapest reliable stop in the four areas.
description: A tea stall on the main Hill Road pavement that has been there for decades, with a bench along the wall and no other seating. Chai, anda bun, and a bun maska. Cash only, sixty rupees, and a queue that moves. This is the record to reach for when a plan has twenty minutes and almost no money left.

name: Neoclassical Cinema, Bandra East
blurb: A single-screen cinema in a red-brick art deco building, with a lift to the balcony and a food court that is better than it needs to be.
description: A restored art deco cinema with three screens-worth of character in one room, an original balcony, and a lift that reaches the upper level. Two hours twenty with a film and a snack is a normal visit, which makes it unusable in a short window. Step-free, hearing loop at the box office, toilets on site.

__meta.note: `accessibility.hearingLoop: true` is inferred, not surveyed. 140 minutes is deliberate: this is the record the duration gate must reject in any window under 150 minutes with travel.

name: Bandra West covered market hall
blurb: A roofed market hall on a lane, level throughout, and it is open when the sun is not. The reliable Bandra answer to rain.
description: A permanent roofed market hall of small units: flowers, cloth, dry provisions, a hardware stall, and a food counter. It stays open through the monsoon, which is the whole reason it is in this list. Level floor throughout, wide aisles, a lift to the mezzanine, and public toilets inside.

name: Bandstand sunset yoga
blurb: Free, on the Bandstand terrace, at five. You can sit at the back and just watch the sun go down over the city instead.
description: A volunteer class on the flat stone terrace with the skyline behind it, ending exactly at sunset. Mats on a hard surface, no toilets on site, and about twenty people. Sitting at the back on the wall and watching is a completely legitimate way to spend the hour if you do not want to stretch on stone.

name: Backgammon and chai cafe
blurb: Games on the tables, chai from the counter, and nobody will ask you to leave until closing. This is a rainy-evening answer that is not a restaurant.
description: A ground-floor room where backgammon and carrom tables are free to use and the staff will teach you both. Order at the counter and bring your plate to the table. Level, step-free, no toilets on site, and it fills up with players from four in the afternoon.

name: Goan church choir rehearsal, open door
blurb: Forty-five minutes of unamplified four-part singing behind a side door, on a Saturday, for nothing. Goan polyphony in the room it was written for.
description: A parish choir rehearsing unamplified, with the practice door propped open and visitors welcome to sit at the back. No charge, no collection, and no expectation of anything. The sound in the room is the reason; it is entirely unamplified, so a hearing loop does not exist and a hard-of-hearing visitor will struggle.

name: Pali Hill waterfront benches
blurb: Flat, shaded, benches, and nothing to buy. If you want to sit with a book for forty minutes this is a better answer than a cafe.
description: A stretch of level, tree-shaded public ground by the water with fixed benches and a kiosk that is closed half the time. Bring your own food, because the kiosk is unreliable. No toilets, so it is a poor choice if that need is in the context.

name: Bahar classical dance performance
blurb: A short classical set in a community hall, seventy minutes, with the musicians sitting at the side of the stage.
description: Two dancers and four musicians in a hall rather than a theatre, with a short introduction spoken before the set. The room is flat, the chairs are metal, and the whole thing runs to a hard stop. Children do well from about seven because somebody explains what is happening first.

name: Hill Road craft and metal shops
blurb: A run of small shops selling brass, leather and wood, all of them air-conditioned, all of them the same. It is shopping, not a market, and the prices are the same too.
description: Three or four units selling the same brass and leather work at the same prices, with a fixed list and no bargaining. Useful if you want to actually buy something rather than browse, and there is a cafe on the same row. Level pavements, and the shops are the only part of this record that are indoors.

activities: sitting in the cafe next door

name: Pali Naka night market and bar row
blurb: A junction that turns into a bar street from nine, with a Saturday crowd that fills it by eleven. Two hours, minimum age eighteen, and no step-free entry to most of it.
description: A working junction with roadside bars, a food stall row, and a crowd that peaks on a Saturday. Two hours is realistic: one hour is a drink standing up, two is a meal and a few more. Stairs and kerbs everywhere, which makes it a poor match for anyone who cannot manage either, and the crowd density after eleven is the highest of anything in this file.

__meta.note: Placed under neighbourhood Bandra because the isochrone reference data covers `pali_hill`; the record is geographically Pali Naka. Density and step-free negatives are deliberate so the crowd and low-stairs penalties have real material.
